title: Collapsed or unresponsive crewmate
whenToUse: A crewmate collapses or is unresponsive in front of you.

steps.text: Check for alarms, smoke or chemical fumes. Follow your spacecraft's emergency procedure.
steps.caution: Put on emergency breathing protection first if cabin air may be unsafe.

steps.text: Tap their shoulders firmly and shout loudly to check if they respond.
Alert the crew and medical officer right away and fetch the AED.
Open the airway and check for normal breathing for up to 10 seconds.
steps.detail: Tilt head and lift chin (use jaw thrust if trauma is suspected). Slow gasps are not normal breathing — start CPR immediately.

steps.text: If breathing normally, tether or strap them safely and keep the airway open.
steps.caution: Give nothing by mouth while drowsy or unresponsive; stay with them and recheck breathing every minute.

redFlags: They are not breathing normally or only gasping.
They do not wake up within 1 to 2 minutes or have a head injury.
Cabin air, CO2 or toxic-fume alarms are active.

escalation.text: Red flag or getting worse? Alert a crewmate now. Do not wait for Earth.
